niche: a ticketing marketplace's internal service latency SLIs read from a trace store that keeps whole traces at the edge at an hourly reset keep rate, with December's customer-facing incidents charged to the service whose own handling caused them
answer: Put reliability engineers on places, partner-gateway, fares, seat-map, notifications, in that order: the five ran over their 2026 latency error budgets
analyst_test: A careful run reweights each service's own kept spans hour by hour on its own load balancer count (fares 0.4, partner-gateway 1.1, notifications 0.6) and puts each December incident on the named service furthest over its load curve across the incident (journey-search on 21 December, accounts on 26 December, seat-map on 14 December; fares and notifications 0.9 each): it files places and seat-map, or with the root weights places, seat-map and partner-gateway.
domain_test: The field's own estimation from a cluster sample with unequal, unrecorded inclusion probabilities (each trace's root edge service and hour), cause against symptom in a call tree separated from load, and intervals that match the design; with a hospital's nouns the trace root, the keep share and the call tree have no meaning.
layer1: span timestamps in microseconds since the epoch (UTC) against the SLO year in Lisbon time
duplicate span rows from exporter batch retries
health-check and synthetic canary traffic in the trace store
the edge route report's daily layout change in June
route names templated in one source and raw in another

stakeholder_role: head of platform reliability at a Lisbon intercity bus and ferry ticketing marketplace

spine.entity: one span the trace store kept: a request an edge service handled or a call inside the trace it started
spine.source: synthetic (the tracing store's span export for December 2026)

world.org_type: an online marketplace selling intercity bus and ferry tickets in Portugal and Spain

driver: Several unit-level rates are estimated from a cluster sample whose inclusion probability is set by the stratum each cluster starts in, events are attributed to the unit whose own processing degraded first against its load-matched norm rather than to the first unit reported, the event time is removed only from the units that suffered it, and the intervals carry the clusters and the unequal weights, so the units over their limits need the weighting and the attribution together.
driver_concrete: Each Rotalinha service's December latency SLI is estimated from the trace store's whole-trace edge sample with each kept span weighted by its root edge service's hourly keep share; each December customer-facing incident is put on the service whose own handling slowed first against its load-matched norm, not the service the responders named first; a service's incident time leaves its SLI only where another service was at fault; fares and notifications run over only when the weights and the attribution are both right, partner-gateway only with the weights.
stump: A careful run reweights each service's own kept spans hour by hour on its own load balancer count (fares 0.4, partner-gateway 1.1, notifications 0.6) and puts each December incident on the named service furthest over its load curve across the incident (journey-search on 21 December, accounts on 26 December, seat-map on 14 December; fares and notifications 0.9 each): it files places and seat-map, or with the root weights places, seat-map and partner-gateway.

differentiation.mark245: mark245 rebuilds whole recording periods a failing recorder lost, from each period's driver; here no hour is lost: the store keeps whole traces at a rate each edge service resets hourly, and a span's weight comes from the edge request that started its trace.
differentiation.mark265: mark265 admits units to a survival risk set only from when a late-starting record first saw them; here there is no duration or entry time, only a share of requests in traces kept at an hourly edge rate.
differentiation.mark139: mark139 v1 reads a randomised intervention per assigned unit rather than per recorded case; here there is no intervention or assignment, only an inclusion probability set where each trace starts.
differentiation.mark182: mark182 v4 corrects snapshots that see each item in proportion to its own duration; here inclusion is set by the edge service that started a trace, at a rate its own hourly traffic sets, not by any item's length.
differentiation.mark270: mark270 v1 corrects correlations among members picked in rank order of a weighted sum, and v6 joins sales to landings to place items outside their slot; here nothing is selected on the measured values: a span inherits the keep rate of its trace's edge service, recovered from that service's hourly count in a second system.
differentiation.mark452: mark452 v2 weights reference points by the preliminary stratum they were drawn from after a reclassification; here the inclusion probability is recorded nowhere, belongs to the unit that started the trace rather than the unit measured, and is recovered hour by hour from the load balancer's count.
differentiation.mark264: mark264 weights each sampled person by the inverse of an inclusion probability proportional to their own visit count; here a span's inclusion probability is not its own unit's at all but that of the edge service whose request started its trace, at that service's hourly keep share.
differentiation.task6: v7 keeps v6's world and its root keep-share weighting as one result among six; the services over budget now need the incident attribution as well, and the intervals, the incident minutes and the attribution are graded on their own

lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is how many people are at each small area on a typical day, known completely only as the members attached to each area and observed day by day only in a broad sample whose on-site rate falls with how far a member lives from the area; carrying the sample's rate for each kind of member onto the complete attachments credits the areas that draw their members from far away with too many present, so the rate has to be carried within the groups it varies across.
lineage.architecture: v1 (a quick-commerce grocer's 2027 weekday dark-store pilot among six metros, by each core's delivery-weighted density of people present, the commuting table's flows carried at a national survey's days on the premises)
lineage.fate: spent 2026-10-18 at stage 4: the isolated reader carried the survey's share by industry group and HOMEREL onto every flow by reflex and committed the golden call, Tessavon at 28,805 against Corrisford's 21,709 (score_reader.py exit 1); the stratum was a classifier both sources share, so the careful analyst's first group-by; the judge found the call forced, Gate H passing, and two ask forks

lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is how far each area's stock has fallen, observable either through the records of collectors who choose where to sample by how much they find there or through a fixed probability sample of the whole area; as a stock shrinks it retreats into the best part of its area and the collectors follow it, so their catch per unit of effort holds up while the stock falls and the parts they abandon drop out of their record, and only the fixed sample, weighted over the whole area, shows the fall.
lineage.architecture: v2 (re-rooted 2026-10-18 after architecture 1's stage-4 reader landed the call)
lineage.fate: spent 2026-10-18 at stage 4: the isolated reader went to the autumn survey first and weighted each depth band by its share of the stock area from plan 4.2's estimand and the manual's equal stations per band, committing Halmorie Deep at 63 per cent against Brettach Bank's 52 with every fall (score_reader.py exit 1); a survey whose own manual describes its strata under an estimand filed as a total over an area makes the design-based estimate the careful analyst's default; the judge found the call forced, DETERMINISTIC and APPROVE

lineage.architecture: v3 (registry heart failure survival, the patients lost to a move north carried from their NYHA class at the move)
lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is the share of units still free of an event a fixed time after their start, from a record that loses sight of units once they leave its reach, where units leave far more often after their recorded state has worsened; treating each loss as ordinary censoring credits the departed with the survival of the units still followed, so each departed unit's survival has to be carried from the state it was in when lost, through the moves between states and the state-specific event rates the followed units show.
lineage.fate: spent 2026-10-28: the portal's determinism round failed it with both judges (charter 3.2 read as the deaths on file), and the re-judge after the WHAT repair sent it back: plain Kaplan-Meier a rule-compliant reading naming Fennick (Gate C), the mechanic classed single_conceptual_flip (Gate G); two corrections of one graded quantity

lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is the eventual count of events from a closed period, completed from those reported so far with lag factors taken per reporting route, where the route is built by joining each report's representative to a register of firm types, because one route reports far later than the others and one unit's mix shifted toward it; completing each unit with its own past lag pattern, by event kind or by the coarse reporter field under-counts that unit, and only the route split reproduces an earlier closed period that a past shift in another unit disturbed, as a filed back-test requires.
lineage.architecture: v4 (a motor insurer's 2027 telematics pilot regions by accident-year 2025 claim frequency, the claims not yet notified developed by notifying route, the route built by joining each claim's representative to the representatives table)
lineage.fate: spent 2026-10-31 on the learning loop's paper screen: the route split sits one join away (the notified-by field plus the representatives table) and development by notification channel is the field's own reserving refinement, so the decisive rung is a reflex; one portal determinism return on architecture 3 before it; shipped 2026-10-28 and superseded before a portal result on the author's instruction to rebuild the batch under the survivor anatomy

lineage.driver: The buying unit is a group of member records that no key joins, linked only by a payment card they share in a separate settlement record; read record by record, the share of each rival's buyers who also buy the house offer is lowest for the rival bought mostly by a group's second member, whose partner buys the house offer on another record, while built from the linked groups the lowest share falls on a rival bought by one-member groups.
lineage.driver_concrete: Homes are assembled from Rewards cards and online accounts that pay with the same bank-card token in Faircourt's settlement file; card by card Nordhavn capsule buyers look least likely to buy Corcally's Roastery because their partners buy it on another card, while home by home the lowest overlap is Oro Rosso's, bought by one-person homes.
lineage.stump: A competent analyst takes each Rewards card as one buyer, measures the share of each rival brand's 2026 buying cards that also bought Corcally's Roastery and names Nordhavn, where Nordhavn's capsule buyers are mostly a home's second card whose other member buys the Roastery; assembled from the cards and online accounts that share a payment card in the acquirer's settlement file, homes put Oro Rosso lowest and Nordhavn mid-table.
lineage.architecture: v5 (Corcally's Roastery 2027 sampling: the rival whose buying homes least often also bought the Roastery, homes assembled from Rewards cards and online accounts sharing a bank-card token in the acquirer's settlement file)
lineage.fate: spent 2026-11-07 at its first portal round: both responses named Oro Rosso, the golden, each building homes through the settlement file's shared card reference; filing the unit as the home announced the linkage, and leaving it unfiled forks the call

lineage.architecture: v6 (Rotalinha's internal services over their 2026 latency error budget, each kept span weighted by its trace root's hourly keep share)
lineage.fate: returned 2026-11-09 at final review (version 17, every platform check passed): one thing, the root keep-share weight decided partner-gateway alone (1.4 to 2.9 per cent against 2.0, four services over to five); re-rooted to a results chain in the same world on the reviewer's own direction
lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is the share of a unit's events beyond a line, read from a store that keeps or drops whole chains of events by a decision taken where each chain starts, at a rate reset every hour from that starting unit's last hour of traffic; a downstream unit's kept events carry the inclusion probability of the unit that started their chain, recovered from that unit's hourly count in a separate usage record, and reweighting them by their own unit's hourly keep share under-weights the busiest upstream caller, whose calls are the slow ones.
lineage.driver_concrete: Each internal service's December latency SLI weights every kept server span by the inverse of its trace's keep rate, the share of requests the edge service that started the trace kept that hour against the load balancer's count of them, because the trace store keeps or drops traces whole at the edge; partner-gateway's slow availability lookups come from journey-search's searches, kept at the smallest rate, so reweighting partner-gateway's spans hour by hour by its own count, or not at all, passes it.
lineage.stump: A competent analyst who sees the trace store's sample thin in the busy hours reweights each service's kept server spans hour by hour by that service's own load balancer count, which lands the edge services, and passes partner-gateway, whose spans were kept with the traces that journey-search, seat-map and booking started at very different rates; journey-search's searches, which make partner-gateway's slow availability lookups, are kept at the smallest rate, so weighted by each trace's own edge keep rate partner-gateway breaches its 2 per cent budget.
